$comment: Preorder campaigns per Shopify SKU, read by app/lib/preorder-campaign.ts and, for the words pages show, app/lib/sales-model.ts (the table of what lives where is at the top of that file). stockFrom names the place paid stock is held, per locale (French also as "en Belgique" and "depuis la Belgique", which the article decides); pages and copy ({{stock_from}}) read it from here. A product line whose preorder ships on its own date sets `ships` on its batch, as "ships by 31 May 2027": site-wide lines then name the latest ship-by date of any preorder. Batches are in production order: a paid batch is stock Incutec already ordered and carries its own ship promise; any other batch is a funding target whose supplier order is placed once that many units are ordered. Set `ships` on a batch once its supplier order is placed. `reserved` on a paid batch holds that many of its `units` back from sale (review units), so customers buy at most `units` less `reserved` and every batch count, ship promise, paid-batch cap and batch tag uses that sellable cap, while price steps and funding targets count paid customer units only. Only SKUs the Shopify catalog policy sells as preorder are affected. countFrom is the first day whose paid Shopify orders count. priceTiers is how the price steps per SKU as paid units come in, and a SKU may set its own priceTiers in place of it: upTo is the step's last unit and off its share off the Shopify compare-at price (the retail price). Past the last step a unit costs retail. app/lib/shopify-price-tier.ts writes each step to Shopify; a SKU Shopify still prices under its step closes until it is written. shipsBy is the one ship-by date of every funding-target unit, however early its target is reached. pendingShips is the ship promise for a funding-target unit: it must name endsOn and shipsBy; app/lib/preorder-campaign.test.ts checks both. A confirmed campaign leaves pendingShips out: the parser writes it from shipsBy ("ships by" and the date), so the ship-by date is typed here once. A SKU's last batch has no end when it is a funding target: its units are the target, and once it is reached every later unit ships with it. endsOn is the target deadline, the end of that day in Europe/Brussels: a buyer whose target is missed by then chooses a refund or to keep waiting, and from then on a SKU whose next unit would wait for a funding target that is not yet reached closes (paid stock, a batch with its own ships date and a reached target keep selling, the product page then reads "Pre-order target reached"). shipsWith lists SKUs that ship with a campaign SKU (accessories, spares): a flat Shopify price with no steps, units that do not count toward the lead, and the lead batch named in `batch` (one with its own ships date, or a funding target the SKU then waits for) or, without `batch`, the batch the lead's next unit falls into. With `stock` (units on hand) and `after`, the first `stock` paid units of the SKU ship with `batch` and later ones with lead batch `after`. Prices live in Shopify, never here. deliveryBy is the separately reviewed final customer delivery date for each batch; the ship promise names it, and null leaves it out. regions lists where a batch ships, EU, US, NEAR (UK, Switzerland, Norway: import VAT and duties paid by the buyer on delivery) or INT (absent: every region, except a paid batch, which takes paidRegions). paidRegions is the one entry for where paid stock in Belgium ships: the EU only (founder 2026-11-03: the batch 1 cap is the safe physical stock and is EU only); NEAR, INT and US buyers take the March funding batch. Shipping stock to NEAR needs its own allocation pool in code first (not a batch inserted here, which would renumber batch tags). Paid stock is consumed only by orders whose every line ships with it (a campaign SKU with a paid batch, or a shipsWith SKU pinned to one, a stocked one while its units fit the stock): an order with any other line, a motor, frame, receiver, prop or other March item, belongs entirely to the first funding batch, boards included (founder 2026-11-01); price steps and funding targets still count every paid unit. Every other paid unit takes the first batch with room that serves its region, the region being the order's shipping country (EU member, US, GB/CH/NO as NEAR, else INT): a US unit skips an EU-only batch for the next one that serves the US, and the batch counts, ship promises, paid-batch caps and batch tags all follow that allocation, while price steps and funding targets count every region. A SKU's last funding batch must serve every region. deliveryByUS is the reviewed delivery date for a US buyer (shipped direct by the fulfilment partner, duties included); a US promise names only it, and without it leaves the delivery date out. A shipsWith SKU pinned to an EU-only batch, or selling from stock, ships US units with `after` when that serves the US, otherwise with the lead's next US batch. usStock is what a US buyer's unit of any SKU not listed here follows (an in-stock item, a preorder outside the campaign): it ships with that US-serving batch of a campaign SKU, on the same promise, and Belgian stock stays EU only. deliveryByINT is the separately agreed arrival deadline for new international funding-batch orders. The usStock rule also serves INT accessories from the March batch. International shipping charges are confirmed by Shopify at checkout; no flat rate is configured here. US sales open only with PUBLIC_US_SALES and the rate in us-sales.json. confirmed (founder 2026-11-11, terms 2.9): true means every funding batch is produced whatever its count, so no unit waits for a target: the promise is unconditional (written from shipsBy), meters read as a confirmed batch and no SKU closes for a missed target. afterEndsOn is the ONE value for what happens to those batches after endsOn: "closed" (ordering stops), "retail" (ordering stays open at the retail price from the day after endsOn, no price step) or "earlyBird" (ordering stays open and the price steps keep running). soldUnder lists, oldest first, what orders created before each `before` instant were promised: pendingShips (the promise text those orders carry; one that names a target is still recognised and reads as the confirmed batch), paidShips and paidDeliveryBy (paid stock: an order sold with a delivery date keeps it), shipsBy and the funding delivery days when they differed. The last entry's `before` is the end of the publication day of terms 2.9 in Brussels: set it together with the version line of the terms on the day they are published. inStock on a paid batch: the units are on hand in Belgium and ship within a few working days, so the batch has no ship month and no delivery date of its own (terms 7.1 govern). choiceFrom (absent until then) is the UTC instant the buy now or pre-order choice went live, set in the same PR as BATCH_CHOICE = "1": from then on an order line of a board's Pre-order variant is a March unit (README "Buy now or pre-order").
